newsitem.title: USA: Clinton signs law to free up planes for wildfires.
newsitem.headline: Clinton signs law to free up planes for wildfires.

text.p: President Clinton Monday signed legislation allowing the Defence Department to sell excess military aircraft to private contractors for use in fighting forest fires.

Under the Wildfire Suppression Aircraft Transfer Act of 1996, aircraft sold by the military for this purpose would be reconfigured as air tankers leased to the Forest Service to "drench fires from the sky," Clinton said.
He made the announcement from a stage set up in the parking lot of a hotel where he is practicing for his Wednesday night debate against Republican challenger Bob Dole.
It is minor legislation that would not normally rate a presidential appearance but the event allowed Clinton to appear on television looking concerned about regional issues.

"This has been the worst year for wildfires in nearly four decades," he said, adding that the federal government must ensure that Forest Service firefighters "have the very best possible equipment at their disposal."

The Forest Service has primary responsibility for fighting fires in the wild. Privately owned tanker aircraft, which release fire retardants from the air, are a major component of the Forest Service's firefighting capability.

Clinton said the law approved by the Republican-led Congress was necessary because the current fleet of airtankers was antiquated, with most planes dating back to the Second World War or the Korean War.
